summary: Covers eight smaller US federal reward programmes. FinCEN's AML/sanctions programme has taken tips since 2021 (new laws 2021 and 2022) but has paid no awards; its April 2026 proposed rule gives the only statistics (tips and award applications by year, 2021-2024). NHTSA has one published award ($24.3 million, Hyundai/Kia, 2021) and final rules from 2025. DOJ's Corporate Whistleblower Awards Pilot (2024) reports over 1,800 tips but no awards; the Antitrust Division/USPS programme (2025) paid its first $1 million award in January 2026. APPS, wildlife rewards, the lapsed Treasury kleptocracy pilot and the FIRREA declarations provision are documented by statute, with few or no published numbers.

program_rules.applies_to: net amount of the fine, penalty, or forfeiture collected
program_rules.quote: The Secretary may not award more than 25 per centum of the net amount of the fine, penalty, or forfeiture collected or $150,000, whichever is less.
program_rules.notes: Whichever is less of 25 percent or $150,000.

program_rules.applies_to: per reward
program_rules.quote: The Secretary may not award more than 25 per centum of the net amount of the fine, penalty, or forfeiture collected or $150,000, whichever is less.
The Secretary may pay a reward to an individual who provides original information

program_rules.quote: in an aggregate amount equal to not more than 30 percent, in total, of what has been collected of the monetary sanctions imposed in the action or related actions
program_rules.notes: AML Act of 2020 version: no minimum, and awards 'subject to ... amounts made available in advance by appropriation Acts'. Covered BSA actions only (subchapters II and III of chapter 53).

program_rules.quote: under this subchapter or subchapter III that results in monetary sanctions exceeding $1,000,000

program_rules.notes: Payment itself is mandatory ('shall pay') when conditions are met; the amount within the range is discretionary. Same text in the 2023 edition.

program_rules.applies_to: collected monetary sanctions in a covered or related action
program_rules.quote: not less than 10 percent, in total, of what has been collected of the monetary sanctions imposed in the action or related actions
program_rules.notes: Added by the AML Whistleblower Improvement Act (Pub. L. 117-328, 29 Dec 2022), which also extended coverage to sanctions (IEEPA, TWEA) and Kingpin Act violations. FinCEN says it will pay awards only after a final rule (usa-fincen-wb-page-2026).

program_rules.notes: The Secretary 'may' pay, with the concurrence of State and the Attorney General.

program_rules.applies_to: first $1,000,000 recovered (then 10-20% of the next $4,000,000 and 5-10% of the next $5,000,000)
program_rules.quote: The declarant shall be entitled to 20 percent to 30 percent of any recovery up to the first $1,000,000 recovered, 10 percent to 20 percent of the next $4,000,000 recovered, and 5 percent to 10 percent of the next $5,000,000 recovered.
program_rules.notes: Sliding scale; nothing is payable on recoveries above $10,000,000 under this formula. Enacted by the Financial Institutions Anti-Fraud Enforcement Act of 1990 (Pub. L. 101-647).

program_rules.applies_to: first $1,000,000 recovered
program_rules.quote: The declarant shall be entitled to 20 percent to 30 percent of any recovery up to the first $1,000,000 recovered

program_rules.applies_to: share of a civil recovery ('shall have the right to share'); rewards for criminal convictions are discretionary
program_rules.quote: the declarant shall have the right to share in the recovery as follows
program_rules.notes: Mandatory share of civil recoveries; separately, 4205(c) lets the Attorney General 'in his discretion' pay a reward after a criminal conviction.

cases.target: Hyundai Motor America, Inc.; Kia Motors America, Inc.
cases.summary: NHTSA's first whistleblower award: information on Hyundai and Kia's late Theta II engine recalls and inaccurate reporting led to two consent orders (23 Nov 2020). Award of the maximum 30 percent of the civil penalties collected, plus 30 percent of any 'Performance Obligation Amount' collected later.
cases.quote: million and three hundred thousand dollars ($24,300,000). 3 This award is the maximum allowable thirty percent (30%) of the civil penalties that have been collected by the United States pursuant to the Consent Orders.
cases.notes: Whistleblower Award Request No. 2021-0001. The quote starts mid-sentence ('twenty-four' is on PDF p. 1) and the '3' is a footnote marker. Collected penalties per the order: Hyundai non-deferred $54,000,000 and Kia non-deferred $27,000,000 (PDF p. 3); abeyance and performance-obligation amounts not collected at the time. Date from NHTSA's award table (usa-nhtsa-wb-page-2026). The whistleblower, Kim Gwang-ho (Gwang-Ho Kim), a former Hyundai engineer in South Korea, went public himself (Reuters, 12 Nov 2021, cited in the final rule, footnote 11); name from usa-taf-nhtsa-rules-2024.

cases.target: Hyundai Motor America; Kia Motors America
cases.summary: Press release on the same award: more than $24 million, the maximum percentage of $81 million paid in cash out of $210 million in combined consent-order penalties.
cases.quote: NHTSA will give more than $24 million to a whistleblower in connection with information provided to NHTSA related to Hyundai Motor America (Hyundai) and Kia Motors America (Kia). This award is the maximum percentage allowed by law of the $81 million in cash collected by the United States
cases.notes: Same award as usa-nhtsa-wb-2021-0001, as the press release describes it ('more than $24 million' is a lower bound; the order says $24,300,000). sanctions_amount is the cash collected; combined penalties were $210 million. award_pct 30 from 'maximum percentage allowed by law' and the release's statement that the maximum is 30%.

cases.summary: First award under the Antitrust Division/USPS Whistleblower Rewards Program: tip led to criminal antitrust (bid rigging) and wire-fraud (shill bidding) charges resolved by a deferred prosecution agreement over used-vehicle online auctions.
cases.quote: a $1 million reward to a whistleblower who provided information that led to EBLOCK Corporation resolving criminal antitrust and fraud charges through a deferred prosecution agreement, under which it has agreed to pay a $3.28 million criminal fine
cases.notes: Press release 26-71 (C.D. Cal.). Percentage not stated. The Division describes the scheme as a '$16 million scheme'. Paid about six months after the programme started, per the Chief Postal Inspector's quote.

cases.target: Aquarosa Shipping A/S (owner, operator and chief engineer of the M/V Aquarosa)
cases.summary: Court order on a contested APPS whistleblower award after convictions for discharging waste oil and plastic and falsifying records; the court also rejected the whistleblower's attorney's contingency fee claim.
cases.quote: The court found that a substantial award of $550,000 was appropriate to provide a sufficient incentive for seamen to inform the United States of MARPOL violations.
cases.notes: United States v. Aquarosa Shipping A/S, No. 11-CR-00652 (D. Md.). The fine is not given in the bulletin. The bulletin's text layer has stray spaces inside words (OCR), so the quote may need a loose match.

events.title: BSA informant rewards enacted
events.description: 31 U.S.C. 5323 'Rewards for informants' lets Treasury pay up to 25 percent (max $150,000) for information leading to BSA recoveries over $50,000.
events.quote: (Added Pub. L. 98–473, title II, §901(e), Oct. 12, 1984, 98 Stat. 2135.)

events.title: Anti-Money Laundering Act of 2020 rewrites the BSA whistleblower provision
events.description: Section 6314 of the AML Act (in the FY21 NDAA) replaces the old informant rewards with awards of up to 30 percent of sanctions over $1 million, subject to appropriations.
events.quote: On January 1, 2021, Congress enacted the FY21 NDAA, which included the AML Act as a component.

events.title: AML Whistleblower Improvement Act
events.description: Extends the programme to sanctions (IEEPA, TWEA) and Kingpin Act violations, sets a 10 percent minimum award and creates the Financial Integrity Fund.
events.quote: The AML Whistleblower Improvement Act mandated that eligible whistleblowers receive a minimum of 10 percent of monetary sanctions collected in covered actions or related actions

events.title: FinCEN bulletin seeks fraud-related tips
events.description: First whistleblower bulletin, asking for tips on BSA and sanctions violations linked to fraud.
events.quote: FinCEN Whistleblower Bulletin: Blow the Whistle on Fraud-Related AML and Sanctions Violations

events.title: FinCEN proposes rule to pay whistleblowers
events.description: FinCEN submits its proposed whistleblower rule to the Federal Register (10-30 percent awards).
events.quote: Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) submitted to the Federal Register a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM)

events.title: Whistleblower NPRM published
events.description: Proposed 31 CFR 1010.930 published; comments due 1 June 2026. No awards are paid until a final rule.
events.quote: Written comments on this proposed rule must be submitted on or before June 1, 2026.

events.title: FinCEN: awards only after a final rule
events.description: FinCEN's programme page says it will begin processing and paying awards once the implementing regulation is final; no award has been paid under the 2021 law.
events.quote: Once that regulation is finalized, FinCEN will begin processing and paying awards.

events.title: FinCEN bulletin seeks Iran-related tips
events.description: Bulletin asking for tips on Iran-related BSA and sanctions violations.
events.quote: FinCEN Whistleblower Bulletin: Blow the Whistle on Iran-Related Illicit Finance

events.title: Motor Vehicle Safety Whistleblower Act (FAST Act)
events.description: Adds 49 U.S.C. 30172: awards of 10-30 percent of collected sanctions over $1 million to auto-industry employees and contractors; awards allowed before regulations.
events.quote: (Added Pub. L. 114–94, div. B, title XXIV, §24352(a), Dec. 4, 2015, 129 Stat. 1716.)

events.title: NHTSA's first whistleblower award ($24.3 million)
events.description: NHTSA announces its first award, the statutory maximum of 30 percent of $81 million collected from Hyundai and Kia over Theta II engine recalls.
events.quote: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration today announced it is making its first ever whistleblower award.

events.title: NHTSA proposes whistleblower rules (49 CFR Part 513)
events.description: Proposed rule implementing 49 U.S.C. 30172.
events.quote: All comments should be submitted early enough to ensure that the Department of Transportation Docket Management receives them not later than June 13, 2023.

events.title: NHTSA final whistleblower rule
events.description: Final 49 CFR Part 513 published, effective 16 Jan 2025: forms, anonymous filing through a legal representative, 90-day claim window.
events.quote: Effective date: This rule is effective January 16, 2025.

events.title: NHTSA delays enforcing the whistleblower rule to 20 March 2025
events.description: Notice of enforcement discretion so new officials can review the rule.
events.quote: will not enforce the requirements of the final rule titled ‘‘Implementing the Whistleblower Provisions of the Vehicle Safety Act’’ until March 20, 2025.

events.title: DOJ Corporate Whistleblower Awards Pilot Program starts
events.description: Three-year pilot paying awards from forfeited assets for tips on corporate crime in four initial areas (financial institutions, foreign corruption by non-issuers, domestic corruption, private health-care fraud).
events.quote: Starting August 1, 2024, whistleblowers can submit original information to DOJ’s Criminal Division about certain types of corporate crime

events.title: CWA pilot expanded to new priority areas
events.description: Criminal Division memo adds subject areas including cartels and transnational criminal organisations, immigration violations by companies, sanctions, procurement fraud and trade/tariff fraud.
events.quote: effective immediately, I am directing the following amendments to the Criminal Division’s Corporate Whistleblower Awards Pilot Program to reflect priority areas of focus.

events.title: CWA pilot guidance revised
events.description: Revised guidance: eligibility under another whistleblower programme no longer automatically bars an award (only duplicate awards are excluded); submissions through a new online intake portal.
events.quote: being eligible for another whistleblower program no longer automatically renders a whistleblower ineligible for an award

events.title: New CWA intake portal; over 1,800 tips since launch
events.description: DOJ fact sheet reports over 1,800 tips in two years and a new intake portal. No award has been announced.
events.quote: This month, we unveiled a new intake portal to improve the efficiency of the program

events.title: Antitrust Division, USPS and USPS OIG sign whistleblower rewards MOU
events.description: MOU lets the Postal Service pay rewards out of criminal antitrust fines in cases affecting the mail.
events.quote: This MOU becomes effective on the latest of the three dates it is signed by the Parties

events.title: Antitrust Whistleblower Rewards Program launched
events.description: Programme announced in July 2025 (month from a law-firm alert).
events.quote: Launched in July 2025 as a partnership between the Division and Postal Service

events.title: First antitrust whistleblower award ($1 million)
events.description: $1 million reward for information leading to EBLOCK Corporation's deferred prosecution agreement and $3.28 million fine.
events.quote: The Antitrust Division today announced its first-ever whistleblower reward

events.title: Kleptocracy Asset Recovery Rewards Act enacted
events.description: FY21 NDAA creates a three-year Treasury pilot paying up to $5 million per reward for information leading to recovery of stolen assets linked to foreign corruption.
events.quote: There is established in the Department of the Treasury a program to be known as the

events.title: Kleptocracy rewards pilot launched
events.description: Treasury launches the pilot (March 2022).
events.quote: The pilot program launched in March 2022, and the program lapsed on January 1, 2024.

events.title: Kleptocracy rewards pilot lapses
events.description: Statutory sunset three years after enactment; Treasury stopped accepting information.
events.quote: The Kleptocracy Assets Recovery Rewards program lapsed on January 1, 2024.

events.title: House committee reports bill to revive kleptocracy rewards (H.R. 5344)
events.description: Financial Services Committee reports H.R. 5344 (introduced 15 Sep 2025) to re-establish the programme.
events.quote: to amend the Kleptocracy Asset Recovery Rewards Act to extend the Kleptocracy Asset Recovery Rewards Pilot Program

events.title: Financial Institutions Anti-Fraud Enforcement Act of 1990
events.description: Lets private persons file confidential declarations of bank-fraud violations with the Attorney General and share in recoveries.

programs.name: FinCEN Whistleblower Program (AML and sanctions)
programs.notes: Run by FinCEN's Office of the Whistleblower under 31 U.S.C. 5323 (AML Act of 2020, sec. 6314; AML Whistleblower Improvement Act, Dec 2022). Tips on Bank Secrecy Act, sanctions (IEEPA, TWEA) and Kingpin Act violations leading to Treasury or DOJ actions with sanctions over $1 million can earn 10-30 percent of what is collected, paid from the Financial Integrity Fund. FinCEN accepts tips but has paid no awards: it says it will start once its rule is final (proposed 1 April 2026). It publishes no annual report; tip counts come from the NPRM's economic analysis. A smaller informant-reward provision (up to 25 percent, max $150,000) existed in the same section from 1984 to 2020.

programs.name: NHTSA Whistleblower Program (motor vehicle safety)
programs.notes: 49 U.S.C. 30172 (FAST Act 2015). Employees or contractors of vehicle makers, parts suppliers or dealers whose original information leads to a resolved NHTSA/DOJ action with sanctions over $1 million can get 10-30 percent of collected sanctions. Rules at 49 CFR Part 513 effective 16 Jan 2025. One award to date in NHTSA's published list: $24.3 million (Nov 2021, Hyundai/Kia). No annual report found.

programs.name: DOJ Corporate Whistleblower Awards Pilot Program (CWA)
programs.notes: Criminal Division pilot (three years from 1 Aug 2024), run by the Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section, paying awards out of forfeited assets under 28 U.S.C. 524(c): up to 30% of the first $100 million of net proceeds forfeited and up to 5% of $100-500 million, if forfeiture exceeds $1 million. Subject areas widened in May 2025. Over 1,800 tips by August 2026; no award announced (claim forms 'available soon').

programs.name: Antitrust Division Whistleblower Rewards Program (with USPS)
programs.notes: Partnership of DOJ's Antitrust Division, the Postal Inspection Service and the USPS Inspector General (MOU of May 2025). Original information on criminal antitrust and related offences affecting the Postal Service that leads to a fine or recovery of at least $1 million: presumptive award 15-30 percent of the fine, paid by USPS from the part of the fine remitted to it. First award: $1 million (Jan 2026).

programs.name: Act to Prevent Pollution from Ships (APPS) whistleblower awards
programs.notes: Under 33 U.S.C. 1908(a) a court may pay up to half of a criminal fine to the person whose information led to the conviction (often crew members reporting illegal oil discharges); the Coast Guard/EPA may pay up to half of civil penalties. Awards are decided case by case in court; DOJ publishes no totals.

programs.name: Wildlife trafficking rewards (FWS and NOAA; Lacey Act, Endangered Species Act and others)
programs.notes: Several wildlife laws let the Fish and Wildlife Service and NOAA pay rewards from fines and forfeitures; amounts are set by the agency, with no fixed percentage. GAO found 27 rewards totalling $205,500 in FY2007-FY2017 and little publicity. launched = Lacey Act reward clause start ('beginning in fiscal year 1983').

programs.name: Kleptocracy Asset Recovery Rewards Pilot Program (Treasury)
programs.notes: Treasury pilot created by the FY21 NDAA (sec. 9703): rewards up to $5 million (more with the Secretary's personal approval) for information leading to restraint, seizure, forfeiture or repatriation of stolen assets linked to foreign government corruption; $25 million a year cap. Launched March 2022, lapsed 1 Jan 2024. H.R. 5344 (2025) would revive it. No reward payments found. 'ended' is the lapse date; the Treasury page says it no longer accepts information.

programs.name: FIRREA / Financial Institutions Anti-Fraud Enforcement Act declarations (bank fraud)
programs.notes: 12 U.S.C. 4201-4205: a person may file a confidential declaration of bank-fraud violations (FIRREA civil penalties, 12 U.S.C. 1833a) with the Attorney General and is entitled to 20-30% of the first $1 million recovered, 10-20% of the next $4 million and 5-10% of the next $5 million; discretionary rewards after criminal convictions. DOJ publishes no statistics; status unclear.

new_indicators.name: Award applications received
new_indicators.definition: Applications or claims for a whistleblower award received in a period (as opposed to tips).
new_indicators.notes: Needed for FinCEN (NPRM Table 3). Distinct from awards_paid_count and award_claims_denied.

gaps: FinCEN: no annual report to Congress exists (31 U.S.C. 5323 as amended has no reporting duty that I found); the only tip statistics are in the 2026 NPRM (calendar years 2021-2024 plus a 2025 projection). No awards paid; no figure for the Financial Integrity Fund balance found (Treasury budget appendix or monthly statements may show it).
FinCEN: no tip counts by type of violation (BSA vs sanctions) or by country were published.

NHTSA: nhtsa.gov blocks automated access (HTTP 403); its pages and the 2021 award order were read through Wayback Machine captures. No annual report on the whistleblower programme found; only cumulative submission counts (over 150 by April 2023; about 300 by December 2024). The archived 2026 page still lists one award (2021); could not confirm whether any later award or Notice of Covered Action under the 2025 rule exists.

DOJ CWA pilot: no award or published 'successful forfeiture' notice found as of the July 2026 page; only the cumulative 'over 1,800 tips' (Aug 2026). No yearly tip counts, no breakdown by subject area.

DOJ Antitrust whistleblower programme: no tip counts published (officials spoke of a 'frenzy' of interest, per law-firm reports). The official July 2025 launch press release was not found on justice.gov (URL guesses returned 404); the launch month comes from a law-firm alert.

APPS: DOJ publishes no totals of APPS whistleblower awards; only case-by-case court orders and press releases. Several justice.gov press releases returned a bot-check page (bm-verify) and were not read. Only one award (Aquarosa, 2016) is recorded here.
Wildlife rewards: GAO-18-279 PDF download blocked (403); figures read from the GAO product page. No later FWS/NOAA reward statistics found.
Kleptocracy Asset Recovery Rewards Pilot: no data on tips received or rewards paid; the annual reports required by sec. 9703(g) were not found online.
FIRREA declarations (12 U.S.C. 4201-4205): no DOJ statistics on declarations filed or awards paid found.

State Department reward programmes were not covered: those found (terrorism, narcotics, transnational organised crime, war crimes) are bounty programmes, not whistleblower-type, so they are outside this brief.
